executive_summary.question: Under what circumstances does the right of private defence of the body NOT extend to voluntarily causing the assailant's death?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
The right of private defence of the body **does not** extend to voluntarily causing the assailant’s death in the following situations:

1. **The offence is not one of the categories listed in § 38** – i.e., it is not:  
   - an assault that reasonably causes apprehension of death,  
   - an assault that reasonably causes apprehension of grievous hurt,  
   - an assault with the intention of committing rape,  
   - an assault with the intention of gratifying unnatural lust, or  
   - an assault with the intention of kidnapping or abducting.  
   *[§ 39: “If the offence be not of any of the descriptions specified in section 38, the right of private defence of the body does not extend to the voluntary causing of death …”]*【90f8747a-7f40-4ae3-b114-2b216129f432】

2. **The act is done by a public servant (or under his direction) in good faith under colour of office and does not reasonably cause apprehension of death or grievous hurt.**  
   *[§ 37(1)(a)‑(b): no right of private defence against such acts]*【69db30c9-72ad-48eb-b310-9e3137806fa2】

3. **There is time to have recourse to the protection of the public authorities.**  
   *[§ 37(1)(c)]*【69db30c9-72ad-48eb-b310-9e3137806fa2】

4. **The defence would inflict more harm than is necessary for the purpose of defence.**  
   *[§ 37(2): “The right of private defence in no case extends to the inflicting of more harm than it is necessary to inflict for the purpose of defence.”]*【6f639d07-62fa-48e0-a811-5492ff51880e】

In short, the right to cause death is limited to those assaults that raise a reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt (or the specific serious intents listed in § 38); outside those bounds, the defender may only use force sufficient to cause non‑lethal harm.

evidence_analysis.claim_text: The right of private defence of the body does not extend to voluntarily causing the assailant’s death in the following situations.
evidence_analysis.supporting_evidence:
If the offence, the committing of which, or the attempting to commit which occasions
the exercise of the right of private defence, be theft, mischief, or criminal trespass, not of any
of the descriptions specified in section 41, that right does not extend to the voluntary
causing of death, but does extend, subject to the restrictions specified in section 37, to the
voluntary causing to the wrong-doer of any harm other than death.

private defence of the body does not extend to the voluntary causing of death to the
assailant, but does extend, under the restrictions specified in section 37, to the voluntary
causing to the assailant of any harm other than death.
